references.text: The Pharisees went out and plotted how to kill Jesus, after he had healed on the Sabbath – a direct parallel to their anger in Luke 6:11.
Mark's parallel account: After healing the man with the withered hand on the Sabbath, the Pharisees went out and conspired with the Herodians to put Jesus to death.
The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered the council and discussed what they should do about Jesus, just as in Luke 6:11 they debated what they could do against him.
The Jewish leaders persecuted Jesus because he healed on the Sabbath, and they wanted to kill him – showing the same pattern of hostility as in Luke 6:11.
The kings of the earth rise up, and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord and his Anointed – a prophetic parallel to the leaders' hostile plotting against Jesus.
The early church quotes Psalm 2 and applies it to the conspiracy against Jesus, which corresponds with the leaders' plans against him in Luke 6:11.
The people in the synagogue at Nazareth were filled with rage against Jesus and wanted to throw him off a cliff – a similar outburst of anger as that of the Pharisees in Luke 6:11.
The council members became furious and sought to kill the apostles – the same pattern of reckless anger (ἀνοία) that the Pharisees showed toward Jesus.
The chief priests, the scribes, and the leaders of the people sought to have Jesus removed from their midst, which is a continuation of the plans that began already in Luke 6:11.
The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death – the final fulfillment of what began with plotting in Luke 6:11.
